2026-08-18T03:24:36.4029185Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4029881Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4030464Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4031364Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4032023Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4032950Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4037215Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4042253Z >
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4047814Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4053253Z >
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4054941Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4056407Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4056722Z ### How to Use
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4057145Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4058951Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4060329Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4060639Z ```bash
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4061712Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4063044Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4112995Z ```
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4113475Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4114010Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4116021Z ```bash
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4117022Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4118475Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4120020Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4122128Z ```
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4122512Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4123631Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4125440Z ```bash
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4127243Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4128627Z ```
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4129016Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4129810Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4130887Z ```bash
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4131836Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4134490Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4135825Z ```
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4136194Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4136669Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4137441Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4141038Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4144993Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4145309Z ```bash
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4146163Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4147736Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4150080Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4150679Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4151524Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4153487Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4155938Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4156809Z ```
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4157200Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4158616Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4161108Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4161429Z ```bash
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4162755Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4164540Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4165871Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4167503Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4168270Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4169762Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4170766Z ```
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4171212Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4171595Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4181185Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4183024Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4185066Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4187928Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4190053Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4191096Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4191401Z ### Notes
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4191793Z 
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4193626Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4196527Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4199544Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4201923Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4205037Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4207089Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4209545Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4210874Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-18T03:24:36.4211579Z <github-context>
